commits.edited_message:
first cpix implementation

Also recognize ContentKeyUsageRule LabelFilter elements: GPAC does
not filter key assignment by label, so the filter's Label text is
logged and the rule is otherwise applied unconditionally instead of
being rejected as an unsupported filter.

coupling: The defect is split across two real commits that touch the same static helper crypt_xml_get_text() in src/media_tools/crypt_tools.c, and neither diff is wrong by itself. Commit 2366657 ('first cpix implementation') is edited to add support for ContentKeyUsageRule/LabelFilter elements: it fetches the filter's Label text via crypt_xml_get_text() and frees the result. At the point this commit lands, crypt_xml_get_text() returns a freshly gf_malloc'd, concatenated/trimmed copy of the node's text content (the function is introduced in this very commit with that contract), so calling gf_free() on the result is exactly correct and the new call site is fully consistent with its only sibling call sites in the same commit. Commit 00022f9 ('crypt_xml_get_text(): avoid allocation ...') is left completely unedited (its patch is empty - it is included only because its real, original content is the other half of the coupling): it changes crypt_xml_get_text() to return a borrowed pointer directly into the live XML DOM tree (child->name) instead of an allocated copy, and it correctly removes the matching gf_free() calls at the three call sites that exist in upstream GPAC at that time (PlainValue, PSSH, HLSSignalingData). That diff is also fully self-consistent: every caller visible in 00022f9's own diff is updated to match the new contract. Neither commit's diff mentions the other's call site: 00022f9's diff never touches the LabelFilter code (added earlier, in a different commit, for a different feature), so a reviewer scoped to that diff sees three-for-three callers fixed and no reason to suspect a fourth. 2366657's diff is reviewed against the contract it itself defines, where freeing the result is correct. Only by composing the two - knowing that 2366657 added a caller that owns/frees the string, and that 00022f9 later silently changed crypt_xml_get_text() to return borrowed memory without auditing for that caller - does the bug appear: label_text now aliases the XML DOM text node's own `name` field, gf_free(label_text) frees it prematurely, and gf_xml_dom_del()'s later teardown of the same DOM tree frees the identical pointer again. Fixing only 00022f9 (e.g. reverting the contract change) would defeat its stated allocation-avoidance purpose; fixing only 2366657's diff in isolation is impossible without first knowing the later commit changes the callee's contract. A correct fix must either update the LabelFilter call site when applying 00022f9's contract change, or make crypt_xml_get_text() continue to hand out an owned copy - both require reasoning about both commits together.
